proof_summary: At index \(10^k-1\), the final product is a positive multiple of \(10^k-1\); every such multiple has decimal digit sum at least \(9k\) (via base-10 block folding and digit-sum subadditivity), and deleting zeros preserves this sum. Hence every reachable value there is at least \(10^{k-1}\), so the successive minima are unbounded.
